facts.claim: Valuation method: reverse DCF FCF0 $1.25bn, Ke 8.5%, terminal 2.5%, 10 years: implied 5.1% vs base 6.0% = in line
facts.source: Recomputed from release guidance (OCF ~$1.80bn less capex ~$550m) and Yahoo snapshot (market cap $26,083m, 110.37m shares, beta 0.549)
facts.source_value: Reproduces 5.1%. CAPM check: 5.17% + Blume beta 0.70 x 4.14% = 8.06%, so 8.5% is conservative. FCF is before SBC (about $88m TTM) and before the 49% noncontrolling share of the Corewell entity (~$50m a year): after SBC $1,162m implied growth is 5.0% at 8.06% and 6.1% at 8.5%; after SBC and NCI $1,110m, 5.6% and 6.7%. Interest income immaterial (cash $626m)
facts.note: Method is FCF-based and the discount rate is above the Treasury-consistent rate, but the dossier states no ERP and does not deduct SBC. Restated implied growth stays within about 1 point of the 6.0% base, so implied_vs_base = in_line stands.

verdict_changes.why: Reverse DCF with SBC deducted implies ~30%/yr FCF growth vs 22% base and 24% organic revenue growth; valuation is above base, which was the stated reason for INCLUDE-SMALL.

Scenarios used non-GAAP EPS (SBC added back) and no cash-flow DCF; FCF-after-SBC reverse DCF implies 13.6-19.3% growth vs ~10% base (above), GAAP-EPS base return about 3% a year, and H1 FY27 cash conversion fell to 0.83x OCF/NI.
